run.question:
I'm connected to the ci-cd cluster. We got a P1 alert and need help finding the root cause.
Our cluster inventory is in the app-235-cluster-inventory index and deployment/change history
is in the app-235-change-history index. Please search these indices to investigate.
[
  {
    "annotations": {
      "description": "Online Devices count gradual decrease over 8 hours in [clientorg-alpha] [56%] for over 30m",
      "workload": "clientorg-alpha"
    },
    "fingerprint": "xx1234567890abcd",
    "labels": {
      "alertname": "onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease",
      "app": "lambda-dashboard-monitoring",
      "cluster": "us-prod-eks",
      "grafana_dashboard_name": "Production-Performance-Overview",
      "org": "clientorg-alpha",
      "severity": "critical",
      "slack_channel": "sre-alerts-channel"
    },
    "startsAt": "30 minutes ago",
    "status": "firing"
  }
]
The alert started right after a deployment. Can you check what's the root cause?

report.summary: The alert payload describes onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease for workload clientorg-alpha, app lambda-dashboard-monitoring, cluster us-prod-eks (severity critical, startsAt '30 minutes ago', i.e. roughly 2026-11-21T04:58Z against the 05:28:04Z window end). Nothing in the connected data carries that identity: the connected Kubernetes cluster's namespaces are app-282, default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo (no ci, no clientorg, no lambda-dashboard namespace), all 26 deployments report ready==available==replicas and all 34 pods are Running/ready, and the only in-window change records are three ci-cd namespace=ci entries (jenkins version bump 2026-11-20T23:27:52Z, argocd-server v2.9.2->v2.9.3 2026-11-21T00:27:52Z, gitlab-runner scale 2->3 2026-11-21T03:27:52Z), the last of which precedes the alert start by about 1.5 h rather than immediately. The five in-window events are only app-282 startup/scaling Normals plus one Warning FailedToCreateEndpoint for app-282/loki at 2026-11-21T05:28:04Z. Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable for this Run, so error rate, latency and trace evidence for the alerting entity could not be examined. The single object that best fits 'the deployment the alert followed' in the ci-cd inventory is argocd-server, but that link is unverified and no evidence ties it (or any other object) to a device-count degradation. No root cause is asserted.

claims.text: At query time the indices exist with 4 documents in app-235-cluster-inventory (4 docs, 9.7kb) and 6 documents in app-235-change-history (6 docs, 9.7kb).

The complete in-window result for app-235-cluster-inventory (total eq 3) contains three Deployment records, all cluster=ci-cd, namespace=ci: gitlab-runner v16.7.0 with 3 replicas status Running (last_updated 2026-11-21T03:27:52Z), jenkins 2.426.3-lts with 1 replica status Running (2026-11-20T23:27:52Z) and argocd-server v2.9.3 with 2 replicas status Running (2026-11-20T23:27:52Z).

The complete in-window result for app-235-change-history (total eq 3) contains: BUILD-5PW2K6, change_type scale, gitlab-runner 2->3 replicas, changed_by infra-team, timestamp 2026-11-21T03:27:52Z; BUILD-3NR8Y1, change_type deployment, argocd-server v2.9.2->v2.9.3, description 'ArgoCD security patch update', timestamp 2026-11-21T00:27:52Z; BUILD-7X4Q9M, change_type deployment, jenkins 2.426.2-lts->2.426.3-lts, timestamp 2026-11-20T23:27:52Z.

The latest change record inside the authorized window is the gitlab-runner scale at 2026-11-21T03:27:52Z; no change-history document inside the window is timestamped later than that (result total eq 3, all rows returned).

The connected Kubernetes cluster has 8 namespaces: app-282, default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly, otel-demo. There is no namespace ci, which is the namespace of every ci-cd workload in the inventory index.

All 26 Deployments read from the connected cluster have readyReplicas == availableReplicas == spec.replicas (1 or 2), including otel-demo ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping, plus app-282 checkout and loki; none is degraded on replica counts.

All 34 pods listed are phase Running with container ready=true; restart counts observed are 0-1 for most pods and 2 on metrics-server-5974bfdbc4-jzqvf, kube-state-metrics-7cbf5b996-df4sz and local-path-provisioner-75f7fc7dc5-qv9jh, and 3 on prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn; no pod is shown Pending, Failed, Evicted or CrashLooping.

Only five events fall inside the authorized window: Normal Deployment ScalingReplicaSet x2 and Normal ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate x2 in namespace app-282, plus one Warning Endpoints FailedToCreateEndpoint; 11 further events were dropped as outside the window.

The only warning event is 'Failed to create endpoint for service app-282/loki: endpoints "loki" already exists' (Endpoints, Warning) at 2026-11-21T05:28:04Z, the same instant at which Deployment checkout and Deployment loki were scaled from 0 to 1 and pods checkout-698c8f5df-c5zlc and loki-66445c6d6f-9mmh4 were created.

The app-282 Deployments read are checkout (containers python:3.9-slim running /app/app.py plus grafana/promtail:2.9.0, limits cpu 100m / memory 128Mi) and loki (grafana/loki:2.9.0, limits cpu 50m / memory 128Mi), both with metadata.creationTimestamp 2026-11-21T05:28:04Z, i.e. created at the very end of the authorized window.

The otel-demo ConfigMap flagd-config defines fault-injection flags productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad, each with state ENABLED but defaultVariant 'off' in the manifest read, so no fault variant is selected by the declared defaults.

The cluster's Prometheus ConfigMap (otel-demo/prometheus) defines alerting rule CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh for cluster opspilot-m1 / namespace otel-demo / service checkout (traces_span_metrics_calls_total status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR over span_name ~.*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, threshold >0.5 for 2m) plus OpsPilotAgentAbsent and OpsPilotModelCallsFailing self-alerts; no onlineDevices/device-count alerting rule appears in that file.

No component-level failure is visible in the connected cluster during the window: every Deployment has ready==available==desired replicas, every pod is Running/ready, and the only Warning event is the app-282/loki duplicate-endpoint message at the window's final instant.

The alerting workload (clientorg-alpha / lambda-dashboard-monitoring / us-prod-eks) is not represented in the connected ci-cd cluster data at all: the live cluster's namespace, deployment and event inventory contains no such workload, and the only change records in the window belong to namespace ci on cluster ci-cd. The degradation therefore most likely originates in an environment whose telemetry is not integrated in this Run, and its cause cannot be attributed from this evidence.

If the premise 'the alert started right after a deployment' refers to the ci-cd inventory, the only deployment-type change before the alert is BUILD-3NR8Y1, argocd-server v2.9.2->v2.9.3 described as 'ArgoCD security patch update' at 2026-11-21T00:27:52Z (about 4.5 h before the alert payload time); no error, latency or log evidence in this Run ties that deployment to a device-count degradation, so it remains an unverified candidate rather than a cause.

A second, weaker candidate is the gitlab-runner scale 2->3 (BUILD-5PW2K6, 2026-11-21T03:27:52Z), the last change before the alert; it is a replica increase on a different workload with no observed failure, so it is not supported as the cause.

Rejected as a cause of the alert: the app-282/loki FailedToCreateEndpoint warning ('endpoints "loki" already exists') at 2026-11-21T05:28:04Z. It is a reconcile-time duplicate-endpoint condition on a pod created at the window's last instant, occurs after the alert is described as already firing for over 30m, and carries no error evidence for loki or checkout themselves.

Rejected as the cause in the observed state: an active fault-injection flag in otel-demo. The flagd-config manifest read shows every fault flag (including paymentFailure, cartFailure, adFailure, productCatalogFailure) at defaultVariant 'off'; no fault variant is selected by the manifest and no restart with an unchanged pod template is evidenced for these workloads in the window.

Pull monitoring from the alerting environment itself: query the us-prod-eks / lambda-dashboard-monitoring online-device metric for clientorg-alpha over the 8-hour gradual-decline period and list deployments/rollouts of that workload in the 30-60 minutes before ~2026-11-21T04:58Z, since neither is present in the connected ci-cd cluster evidence.

Restore the missing telemetry integrations (Prometheus and Jaeger both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) and the change_history integration, so that error-rate, latency, trace and deployment-timeline evidence can be correlated with the alert instead of inferred from static configuration.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable during this Run: get_metric_names, get_label_values, execute_prometheus_instant_query and metrics_range_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, latency or device-count series (including any ERROR series) could be read; this is unknown, not zero.
Jaeger was unavailable: traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span-level error or latency evidence exists for any service in the window.

The alert's own entity cannot be time-filtered in the inventory index (no timestamp field matched) and no in-window change-history document mentions lambda-dashboard-monitoring, clientorg-alpha, us-prod-eks or onlineDevices: the full-text query over app-235-change-history in the window returned nothing, and that no_data view proves nothing either way.

Documents outside the authorized window are unreadable: app-235-cluster-inventory has 4 documents but only 3 fall inside the window, and app-235-change-history has 6 documents but only 3 inside; the remaining 1 and 3 documents are unknown and could include the deployment that triggered the alert.

Kubernetes objects and Prometheus configmaps were read at query time only; they cannot show the cluster's state at ~04:58Z, and the app-282 pods created at 2026-11-21T05:28:04Z have no readable logs inside the window (all their lines fall after the window end).

Log coverage is limited: an error-filtered query on otel-demo/checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n read 288 lines in the window with no line matching err|error|fail|exception|panic, and the same query on otel-demo/frontend-6c9bc688bf-58jmw read 0 lines; both views were no_data, so the absence of error lines and the absence of frontend output are unproven rather than established.
The change_history integration is listed as not integrated; the investigation relied on the app-235-change-history index instead, whose full contents could not be time-unbounded.

The timing of the alert is taken from the alert payload text ('30 minutes ago' relative to the 2026-11-21T05:28:04Z window end) and was not independently corroborated by any firing-alert series, because Prometheus was unavailable.

content:
{"alertmanager.yml":"global: {}
receivers:
- name: opspilot
  webhook_configs:
  - http_config:
      authorization:[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]        credentials_file: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]        type: Bearer
    max_alerts: 0
    send_resolved: true
    url: http://opspilot-web:8080/intake/alertmanager
- name: opspilot-self
route:
  group_by:
  - alertname
  - namespace
  - service
  group_interval: 1m
  group_wait: 10s
  receiver: opspilot
  repeat_interval: 1h
  routes:
  - matchers:
    - opspilot_self="true"
    receiver: opspilot-self
templates: []
"}

{"relay":"connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]      authenticator: basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]      password: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  - basicauth/prometheus
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - otlphttp/prometheus
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - redis
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - otlp
      - debug
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - periodic:
          exporter:
            otlp:
              endpoint: otel-collector:4318
              protocol: grpc
          interval: 10000
          timeout: 5000
"}

{"alerting_rules.yml":"groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
","alerts":"{}
","allow-snippet-annotations":"false","prometheus.yml":"global:
  evaluation_interval: 1m
  scrape_interval: 1m
  scrape_timeout: 10s
storage:
  tsdb:
    out_of_order_time_window: 30m
otlp:
    keep_identifying_resource_attributes: true
    promote_resource_attributes:
    - opspilot.integration.id
    - service.instance.id
    - service.name
    - service.namespace
    - service.version
    - cloud.availability_zone
    - cloud.region
    - deployment.environment.name
    - k8s.cluster.name
    - k8s.container.name
    - k8s.cronjob.name
    - k8s.daemonset.name
    - k8s.deployment.name
    - k8s.job.name
    - k8s.namespace.name
    - k8s.node.name
    - k8s.pod.name
    - k8s.replicaset.name
    - k8s.statefulset.name
    - container.name
    - host.name
rule_files:
- /etc/config/recording_rules.yml
- /etc/config/alerting_rules.yml
- /etc/config/rules
- /etc/config/alerts
scrape_configs:
- job_name: prometheus
  static_configs:
  - targets:
